name: CalibratedMath
why_it_matters: Reporters need models that flag their own uncertainty in plain language so non-expert readers and editors can judge when to trust or verify a claim.
task_shape: Models answer arithmetic questions and must express their confidence in the answer either as a numerical probability or in natural-language hedges (e.g., 'almost certain', 'low confidence'), which are then scored against actual accuracy.
signals: Directly measures whether verbalized confidence tracks true accuracy, a property crucial for editorial trust.
Limited to arithmetic reasoning, so results may not transfer to open-ended factual or investigative tasks.

source.label: Lin, Hilton & Evans, 'Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words' (arXiv)
